Fisher-Price Loving Family Dollhouse As a new dad with no sisters growing up, I'm fairly new to the whole dollhouse experience. While I would have loved (although not necessarily expected) some karate-chop action in the parent figures, or flamethrower accessories, this is a pretty cool looking fortress, no wait, I mean dollhouse, and my daughter loves it, even if she doesn't understand why GI Joe keeps trying to rappel up to the 4th floor balcony with his grappling hook. .

Seriously though, she really does love this dollhouse. I think it's pretty good for the price, as it's absolutely huge (close to 3 ft tall), but to be honest, I expected a lot more in terms of the "stuff" inside. There is some detail built into the walls, but hardly any furniture pieces that you can move around. There are some family members included, but only parents and baby, who appears to have just come from the hospital. It's a bit like a family just moving into their first apartment, where all they have is a moldy old sofa and some flowers on the wall.

Everything that she wants to play with is, of course, something I have to buy separately. That's a bit annoying, but typical I suppose, although someone with more experience in these sorts of girl-fortresses might know of a better alternative. Practically speaking, Cobra Commander and Skelator could just waltz right in the front door, as there are no missile launchers, so those must come in one of the accessory packs.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Loving Family Dollhouse

hand2mind Rekenrek Pop-Up Learning Activity Center, Math Games for Kids, Abacus for Kids Math, Math Manipulatives, Montessori Materials for Preschool, Kindergarten Homeschool Supplies I love these kits! They are a wonderful and painfree way to get a bit of math learning into our days. We have three of them now and my children love them. It's basically games. I love that everything I need is right here in this box. I have to do no prep whatsoever, which is great. It's perfect for those rough, stress filled days.

Within this kit, you get a storage box that doubles as an easel. The 10 activities are attached to the box by a spirally bound book. Each of the activities are on both sides of the easel, so that children can sit on each side of it and still be able to see. It also comes with 2 mini Rekenreks, 4 double sided dry erase boards, 4 dry erase markers, 20 number cards, 2 spinners, and a guide.

This particular kit taught me the difference between a Rekenrek and an abacus. Sadly, I'd never even heard of a Rekenrek beforehand. Apparently, it's much better for younger children to learn number problems with, since it changes colors every 5 beads, instead of 10. Plus, it's usually just 20 beads total, like the ones in this kit, and great for little hands.

If your child could use extra practice with adding and subtrating, or just working with numbers 1-20, this is a nice kit to try.

3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner

PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12 I'm not at all pleased with this donut kit. I like the idea -- a kit that includes everything needed to make baked, frosted donuts that kids (with supervision) can take on as a fun project. Unfortunately, the execution of the idea was not done well.

The items come in a flimsy cardboard box that is easily dented up in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item sent to child. Inside the box is a set of cheap silicone molds for the donuts, a packet of sprinkles and a sealed packet with the mixes. The sprinkle packet opened up in transit so there were sprinkles everywhere. Inside the sealed packet the frosting mix is in a pouch, but the donut mix is just loose in the pouch. Getting the frosting packet out was a very messy proposition.

Making the mix is simple (needs water and oil). The included silicone molds are very thin and flimsy, and need to be inserted into a muffin pan to minimize the chance of spilling. This is the step kids will need the most assistance with.

But even if the donuts bake properly, they are no treat to eat. The chocolate flavor is not pleasant, and is made even worse by the artificial sweetener aftertaste. The texture is not bad considering these are gluten-free, but the taste is not good to the point where these are barely (and I mean barely!) edible.

Two stars for the overall concept of a donut kit as a fun kid project (both making and decorating) but everything else is a fail.
text_fidelity_b: PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12

Angry Birds - Sling and Smash Track Set Our kids, ages 3-10, went crazy seeing this Angry Birds- Sling And Smash Track Set. The set couldn't be more easy to set up. It comes with a spring loaded sling shot with a slide to propel Red, the Angry Bird into destroying Pig City. The city has 2 buildings that sit on 4 ladders. You can make the city any way you want and stand the green pig anywhere. There are stickers included to make the buildings look more real. Once set up, all you do, is pull back the spring and Red, who has a wheel base, either flies or rolls into the pig city, knocking it down along with the green pig. The play is simple, but after a while, our kids starting begging for paper towel cardboard tubes, toilet paper tubes, Tupperware, plastic cups, building blocks, anything light and stackable to build pig city taller, wider, bigger and more fun.

They began cutting windows into the paper towel tubes, so the green pig could watch the bird coming. Then they began decorating the tubes, along with our small Ziploc and Tupperware containers. Soon, there was a pig city big enough to play targeting the city all day. I should have known what was coming next. I soon heard begging, that they desperately need more pigs for the city and more birds to attack. So, I found Amazon has extra figures- Angry Birds Movie Mini Figure Multi Pack Set A and a Set B. Each Set includes both birds and pigs- 7 total figures. They are not expensive- around $13.00 for each 7 figure set. So, I bought both sets, and the figures are very cute, making them worth buying just for their cuteness alone. Now, what was a simple fun Red Angry Bird attacking a lone Green Pig in a little 2 building Pig City has turned into 14 more Angry Birds and Pigs living in a Pig City Block designed from cardboard tubes, small Tupperware containers, blocks and wood scraps all designed from our children's imaginations. This simple little Set is a Big 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: Angry Birds - Sling and Smash Track Set

text_fidelity_a:
The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games First and foremost, this is a LIVING card game. It is not a COLLECTIBLE card game. Big difference! The latter just means that you can buy new expansions to expand your gameplay / add mechanics / etc. The latter means you have to go and buy packs at the store in order to get newer and better cards. In a collectible card game, a billionaire can go and buy all the packs and have the best deck ever. In this game, everyone who buys the game (and its expansion cards) will be on even footing. I find collectible card games to be somewhat predatory given they're essentially like gambling. Okay, on to the review.

High level message is, not great but not bad either. If you love Lord of the Rings you'll have a better experience. If you're neutral on it, then you're not going to enjoy the complicated grind of learning how to play.

Pros
- Beautiful artwork
- Good use of the LOTR lore in the gameplay and story
- Decent length of games - assume 1 to 1.5 hours
- Pretty good mechanics, once you understand them

Cons
- Phew, this game is complicated. The first sign that it's complicated, is the fact that there are TWO rule books, each of hefty size. This is not the kind of game you whip out on game night with a bunch of casual players. You need other folks who are dedicated to play this game, willing to watch a YouTube video together, or something, and then willing to stumble around for the first hour to get this done.
- So many things to keep track of... there's spinners, dials, tokens... did I mention this game is complicated
text_fidelity_b: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

(Also never played but wanted to) So when I got the box and it was barely larger than two boxes of playing cards i went... Well it did say "tiny" on it. I picked up the rules three times and read through them, trying to figure out the solo player game before going "this is not fun to play solo". However we finally sat down and tried out the Tiny Dino game three players. Playing is rather complex involving a small board, cards, and game pieces. It took way longer than the stated 45 minutes, (and TBF we didn't finish all six rounds. Kids quit wanting to play) but that might be because we kept having to figure out order of play, rules and what cards do what. I like the complexity, but it just wasn't a game either of my kids (huge D&D and strategy gamers) liked. They also like rules to be clear, even if complex. So three stars.
One star off because it is hard to read and see in such a small format. One star off because it is needlessly complex, or at least not laid out easily to understand how to play without investing quite a bit of time. Half a star off because one player rules are stupid.
Game free in exchange for an honest review.
text_fidelity_b: Gamelyn Games Tiny Epic Dinosaurs,12+ years

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

City Fire Station Building Kit, Fun Firefighter Toy Building Set for Kids, with Toy Fire Truck, Helicopter, Best Learning Educational Roleplay STEM Toy Gift for Boys and Girls Age 6-12 (896 Pieces) Lots of LEGO-like bricks for a small price. These are fully compatible, and integrate well with kits you've already got. The carrying case is nice too, with a top that doubles as a LEGO base plate.

The only real difference between these and your standard set of LEGOs is the instruction manual. These are pretty straightforward to build, but unlike a regular LEGO manual where each page tells you where to put 3-5 pieces, each step in this one asks you to put 8-20 pieces on a model. It's substantially more difficult for youngsters.

Overall though, this is fantastic value for your money.

I've bought two of these kits now, and one includes quite a few guns and grenades, which isn't exactly "fireman" material. Some of the pieces in the second kit are also quite a bit more stuck in place, where they should be free-moving.

Stemnex Amazing Steam Engine I would recommend this one more for older children and teenagers because there is over 100 parts here and it may be a bit too challenging for younger kids. Regardless, this is one of the neatest things ever. Kids who love trains will definitely love this. I am reminded of something my dad helped me build for a science fair project when I was in 4th grade, and I won a blue ribbon. The one I had though was made from metal parts and springs and such that he put together from old carburators and such. It looked very much like this one. Working on this made me think of my dad when we built my science project. So this would be perfect, in my honest opinion, for any parents to work on with their kids. You just might make some cool memories. It may also be a good item for kids who are home-schooled and learning about this kind of thing in science.

As for product attributes, the pieces go together easily and the instructions are pretty easy to follow. I recommend possibly not taking the pieces off of the brackets until they are needed, this way they won't get lost. The box is quite large, but just the right size to store away under a bed or raised sofa.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Double-Sided Magnetic Tabletop Art Easel - Dry-Erase Board and Chalkboard We were the unfortunate recipients of this activity set given to us from a family member for a gift. We already have one of those classic standing plastic easels which we love, so this tabletop one is more of a nuisance for us. Trying to be open-minded about making it work since it was gift, I starting exploring it and realized how highly dysfunctional it is. The swinging base bar moves to each side of the board to stand it up, meaning each time you want to use the magnets, you have to swing the bar to the one side and prop it up, and then do that again with the opposite side to use the chalk. This takes some finesse that younger kids will not be able to do very easily on their own. It’s also top-heavy with the paper roll on top, so I took the paper off completely.

Why is a marker included for such young children? No, Melissa & Doug…just NO. I get it for older kids, but not for the starting age of 3. The chalk board side doesn’t have any magnetic capabilities, and also doesn’t have a little tray or spot to keep the chalk organized…did parents not have any input in designing this? Yes, there is a tray on the magnetic side to keep the letters and numbers, but not on the chalk side. The fold-down tray also doesn't have a lid, so good luck keeping your letters and numbers organized in one spot when you want to use the chalk side. Nobody thought it would be a good idea to have a spot for the chalk? Or nobody thought it would be a good idea to magnetize both sides to let a child use the chalk and add some letters or numbers to the same side of the board?? Who approved this?

The magnetic side works fine, but I didn’t even bother to do an inventory of all the letters and numbers before I vetoed this thing and gave up trying to make it work in my child’s room. I honestly don’t have a good spot to even keep it anywhere in my house, and if my kid wants to doodle, we’re heading over to our standing easel (designed with two large trays to keep our chalk and crayons organized). I wish I had a gift receipt. DO NOT BUY THIS!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Double-Sided Magnetic Tabletop Art Easel - Dry-Erase Board and Chalkboard

Little Live Scruff-A-Luvs Cutie Cuts: Shave, Reveal and Style, Plush Rescue Pet - Pink Puppy I see a lot of reviews complaining, but I got this for my 6 year old's birthday and she loves it. No, the fur doesn't really "shave off" it's more like you comb it off and grab it. It takes parental involvement and it's messy, but it's meant to be an experience, which it fully delivers. My daughter did the unboxing and loved finding all the surprises. We "shaved" her pup and gave it a bath in a bowl at my kitchen table. We set up a "drying station" with my hair dryer and a towel. The entire experience was magical and bonding for my daughter and I. We giggled and guessed if we would get the Frenchie or Yorkie and wondered what color it's nails would turn. The bath was fun and a bit messy, and blow drying took a while (mostly mom, she got bored) but her favorite part was grooming the Frenchie (it was easy to tell) and adding the little accessories. The surprise factor was 100% on point. The whole time the suspense was palpable for her. She was guessing the whole time and we came up with names for it.
Don't buy this toy if you can't be bothered to spend an hour playing with your child.
Don't buy this toy expecting a 5-7 year old to do this independently.
This toy is clearly meant for interactive play with an adult.
This toy was a wonderful addition to our homeschooling dramatic play for kindergarten.

If you want a toy that allows you and your child to pretend to own a grooming salon, this toy is perfect. Have everything prepared ahead of time. We put a table cloth down and a bowl of warm water with shampoo, then in a separate area we had the drying and grooming station. Expect to spend at least 45-60 minutes on this adorable experience. It's wonderful for people who enjoy playing with their kids. Our whole family loves it.
text_fidelity_b: Little Live Scruff-A-Luvs Cutie Cuts: Shave, Reveal and Style, Plush Rescue Pet - Pink Puppy
